items.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: Art Tatum on the radio, and Teddy Wilson

ctx.x: Well my mother was a part time night club singer. She usually worked days and sang somewhere in San Diego at least a few nights a week. She always loved singing and she was a good singer. And because of that, and also there were some other, I didn’t come from a musician family in the professional sense, but an uncle was a violinist, and we were certainly a music oriented family, and there were some wonderful 78s that I always remember from my earliest childhood memories, that we had in the home, of course before…

Art Tatum on the radio, and Teddy Wilson, and those, along with some of the early records that I mentioned that we had in the home I think were what — I was still too young to be thinking in terms of doing it, but at least it made that connection. The sound of that music seemed very special. It seemed very important compared to the pop music of the day. But actually I became more interested in classical music as I got older, and I was really primarily interested in trying writing—
